text:
Sam Rinzel is in rare company. Hockey.com's headline: "Rinzel joins Orr, Salming and Howe with five straight multi-assist games." That run, Nov. 12 to 21, produced 12 points, and the Chicago Sun-Times credited his "monster game" for the Blackhawks' first road win, in Calgary.

Our numbers call the hot stretch earned. He has 14 points in his last ten games, where his ice time would predict about 5.8, but he's also getting more chances of his own, on minutes up more than four and a half a night. The power play is the engine: 9 of his 17 points have come with the man advantage, and The Athletic's Mark Lazerus asked whether the power play fixed Rinzel or Rinzel fixed the power play.

Not all of it will hold: the Blackhawks have scored 9.8 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and his 2.38 points per 60 sit well above our talent range of 1.06 to 1.67. But Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked his game last season (carry-ins on 47% of his entries, 93rd percentile for chances from in front of the net), so the role looks real.
